title: What Laser Physics Studies — Fundamentals of Laser Physics
description: This entry covers What Laser Physics Studies as part of the fundamentals of laser physics. In this field, stimulated emission matters because an incoming photon cloning itself off an excited atom, the laser's engine. It is taught at the Foundations level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Laser Physics is the field concerned with Light amplified into coherent beams: how lasers work and what they can do. What Laser Physics Studies belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Stimulated emission — an incoming photon cloning itself off an excited atom, the laser's engine. And Coherence — laser light's single wavelength and locked phase, enabling interference and focus. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Foundations tier.
core_concepts: Stimulated emission: an incoming photon cloning itself off an excited atom, the laser's engine.
Coherence: laser light's single wavelength and locked phase, enabling interference and focus.
key_laws: Einstein relations: absorption, spontaneous, and stimulated emission rates linked by coefficients.
vocabulary: Gain medium: the material amplifying light by stimulated emission.
Beam quality: how tightly the beam focuses, measured by M-squared.
methods: Cavity alignment: overlapping mirrors and gain medium for maximum output.
history: Einstein predicted stimulated emission in 1917; Townes and Schawlow proposed the optical maser in 1958, and Maiman built the first laser in 1960. Gas, semiconductor, and ultrafast lasers followed, making lasers ubiquitous from surgery to telecom.
